searchText: For the tree specification, using something that maps directly to SSZ hashing (it's not hard really, eg. SSZ hashing an array really is just a simple binary tree, with an extra leaf at the top level for the length) actually could be a good idea See allcoredevs discussion; there's benefits in starting to SSZ'ify certain pieces as the Merkle branches all become much more standardized and cleaner Curious to hear other people's thoughts on this. Since ssz is also well defined and includes merklization, it seems that using ssz would simplify the spec and let us lean on existing tools. ~~Currently, there is one way to merkleize, `TRIE()` in the yellowpaper.~~ ~~Is it OK to have two different ways to merkleize things? One way for static lists like code chunks (and maybe transactions and receipts). The other way is for merkleizing "non-linear" things like accounts and storage.~~ Asked ^ in main channel. I posted an example SSZ schema that could be used in the discussion thread for the EIP if anyone wants to take a look. <@!364458974906548225> I did not mean to change the subject from your question. My question was inspired by yours. I think that SSZ may be good for merkleizing static lists like code chunks.
